segments.text: Permanent Knowledge-Base Guide for Sun Tan City Leadership
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: This framework teaches Ask Bubbles how to think when helping Sun Tan City leaders coach, develop, document, and hold employees accountable.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: It is not a form recreation tool and it is not a generic HR guide.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It converts Coaching Forms, Management Diamond examples, EPP templates, DPOA templates, and leadership accountability patterns into a reusable management operating system.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should use this framework to help Salon Directors, Assistant Salon Directors, District Managers, and training leaders create behavior-focused documentation that is direct, respectful, accountable, and aligned with Sun Tan City operations.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Confidentiality and anonymization rule: When generating any output, Ask Bubbles must remove or avoid employee names, dates, locations, customer names, rankings, one-time historical details, and personal information unless the manager specifically provides placeholders for a live document.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Use [Employee], [Manager], [Salon], [Date], and [Metric] placeholders when creating reusable knowledge-base content.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Leadership escalation rule: Ask Bubbles may help draft coaching, EPP, DPOA, follow-up notes, and conversation guides, but any termination, demotion, suspension, sensitive employee matter, or final disciplinary decision must be reviewed by the appropriate Sun Tan City leadership process.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should never replace DM, HR, LP, or senior leadership approval.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should never replace DM, HR, LP, or senior leadership approval.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Core Sun Tan City terms used in this framework:
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: - Coaching Form: A documented coaching tool used for under performance, training plan of action, or re-training.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It should capture the topic, behavior, expectation, practice, and plan for improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Management Diamond: A role-play and difficult conversation tool built around WHAT, HOW, WHY, WHEN, and PRACTICE.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It teaches the employee exactly what behavior is expected, how to do it, why it matters, when it should happen, and then requires practice.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A structured plan used when performance requires formal improvement, a role transition requires structured development, or a leader/employee needs a documented performance path with goals and follow-up.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A disciplinary accountability document used for policy violations, repeated unacceptable conduct, or performance/behavior issues that require formal warning or escalation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Expected non-negotiable client-service behaviors that must be visible in client interactions.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The expected way employees engage, ask questions, make recommendations, educate, and close or plant the seed.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - ASTC: Acknowledge, Support, Temperature Check, Complete the Engagement or Plant the Seed.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: This is the core hesitation-handling process.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - BHOW: The membership/value breakdown tool used to explain benefits, how the membership works, and value to the client.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Routine Mat: The skincare routine mat used to educate clients and recommend a complete skincare routine.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: - Curbside Coaching: Real-time or near-real-time coaching based on observed client interactions.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It is specific, immediate, helpful, and followed by another observation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Coaching exists to improve employee behavior, strengthen client engagement, and protect the Sun Tan City experience.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Coaching is not a lecture and it is not punishment.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It is the manager's tool for turning an observation into a better habit.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A strong Sun Tan City leader coaches because:
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: - employees need to know exactly what successful behavior looks like;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - client experience must be consistent, not dependent on who is working;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - productivity metrics improve only when daily behaviors improve;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - employees deserve clear expectations, practice, feedback, and follow-up;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - coaching prevents small performance gaps from becoming larger accountability issues.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should treat coaching as skill transfer.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The manager should not simply tell the employee what was wrong.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The manager should show the employee what to do next, practice the behavior with them, and follow up to confirm the behavior changed.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: What behavior does the manager need to see instead?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Why does it matter to the client, salon, team, and employee?
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: How should the employee do it in real words or actions?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: When will the manager follow up?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Accountability exists to protect the client experience, the salon culture, company standards, and fairness across the team.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Accountability is not about being harsh.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It is about being clear, consistent, and timely.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A strong Sun Tan City leader holds employees accountable when:
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: - the employee has been trained or coached;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - the behavior affects clients, revenue, standards, safety, attendance, dress code, or team trust;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - the same issue repeats after follow-up;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - an employee chooses not to follow policy, direction, or expected behavior.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Accountability should be documented when a behavior needs to be corrected, monitored, or escalated.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The documentation should preserve facts, not feelings.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Coaching is used when the primary need is development, practice, clarification, or performance improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Discipline is used when the issue is a policy violation, conduct issue, repeated failure after coaching, or unwillingness to follow direction.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "Here is what I need to see going forward."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "I will observe your next two client interactions and follow up."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "This behavior is out of compliance with policy or job expectations."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "Any further violation may result in additional disciplinary action, up to and including termination."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should not over-discipline a skill gap that has not been coached.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should also not under-document a repeated issue or policy violation by calling it "just coaching" when the employee has already been coached or the issue is serious.
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: 1.4 Difference between performance issues and behavior issues

segments.text: A performance issue means the employee is not meeting expected job results or execution standards.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Examples include low Spa %, low Club Close %, low PPTA, weak OTC results, poor client engagement, inconsistent ASTC, failure to use the Routine Mat, weak tours or re-tours, or failure to make relevant recommendations.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: A behavior issue means the employee is choosing or displaying conduct that does not meet company standards.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Examples include attendance issues, dress code issues, disrespect, refusal to follow management direction, policy violations, failure to complete required tasks, inappropriate attitude at the counter, or repeated failure to follow a known expectation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: For example, an employee with low Club Close % may be a performance issue if they need more practice overcoming objections.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: It becomes a behavior/accountability issue if the employee refuses to use ASTC, will not role-play, ignores coaching, or continues the same behavior after repeated follow-up.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should classify issues this way:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Skill gap: coach, demonstrate, role-play, follow up.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Knowledge gap: retrain, provide resources, verify understanding, follow up.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Confidence gap: role-play realistic scenarios, give supportive feedback, observe live interactions.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Effort gap: document expectations, increase follow-up, consider EPP or DPOA depending on history.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Policy violation: use DPOA or escalate according to severity and policy.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Leadership gap: use Management Diamond, EPP, or direct accountability plan depending on impact.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A Sun Tan City manager is responsible for creating clarity, not confusion.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: The manager must not assume that employees know what to do simply because a metric is low or a policy exists.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The manager must inspect, teach, reinforce, and hold accountable.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - observe client interactions, not just reports;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - review Daily Stats, Bonus Viewer, Comp Report, productivity tracking, shift summaries, and coaching history;
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - coach in the moment whenever possible;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - document coaching when a pattern or opportunity exists;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - use follow-up notes to prove whether behavior improved;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - praise publicly when appropriate and correct privately;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - ask for support from the DM or appropriate leader when unsure.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A manager should not simply say, "Get your Spa % up," "Sell more clubs," or "Do better." Those statements do not teach behavior.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: A strong manager says, "Today I need you to recommend Spa Wellness to every eligible client by asking a wellness-based question, demonstrating how it supports their goal, and planting the seed if they do not buy today.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: I will observe your next two client interactions and we will debrief after."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Employees are responsible for participating in their own improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The manager must teach and follow up, and the employee must apply the expectation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - ask questions if expectations are unclear;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - use required tools such as BHOW, ASTC, Routine Mat, and client engagement questions;
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: - follow attendance, dress code, safety, and company policy expectations;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - take ownership of client interactions and productivity results.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should hold both sides accountable: managers must coach clearly and follow up, and employees must demonstrate behavior change.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The performance management ladder teaches Ask Bubbles how to choose the right level of action.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The goal is to solve the issue at the lowest appropriate level while still documenting, following up, and escalating when needed.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles must not treat the ladder as automatic in every situation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Serious policy violations may move directly to DPOA or leadership review.
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: 3.1 How coaching forms should be completed

segments.text: A coaching form should capture one main coaching focus.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Multiple topics may be selected if they are connected, but the form should not become a long list of every mistake.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Strong coaching is specific enough that the employee knows what to do differently on the next interaction.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A complete coaching form should include:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Type of coaching: under performance, training plan of action, or re-training.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Topic of coaching: the exact behavior or skill being coached.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Observation: what was seen, heard, or identified in metrics.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Expectation: what behavior must happen going forward.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Why it matters: client experience, revenue, culture, salon standards, or employee success.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: - Demonstration: the correct verbiage or action shown by the manager.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Practice: the role-play or exercise completed.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Follow-up: when and how the manager will verify improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Acknowledgement: employee and supervisor confirmation that the coaching and plan were discussed.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should avoid coaching forms that only say:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should convert those into observable, behavior-focused documentation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should structure coaching conversations in this order:
segments.label: methodology

segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Going forward, I need you to [specific behavior]."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Here is the verbiage I want you to use..."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Let’s role-play that with a client who says [objection/scenario]."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Tell me what you are going to do differently on your next interaction."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "I will observe [number] interactions today and we will debrief before the end of your shift."
segments.label: methodology

segments.label: methodology

segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Employee responded to coaching by rolling eyes, crossing arms, and saying they were not going to use that verbiage" is documentable.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Expectations should be simple, specific, and repeatable.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "For every eligible client today, I need you to use at least one open-ended question, make a relevant recommendation based on their answer, use ASTC if they hesitate, and either complete the engagement or plant the seed.

segments.text: The Management Diamond turns a difficult conversation or skill gap into a teachable structure.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: It prevents vague coaching by forcing the manager to define the exact behavior expected.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The Management Diamond has five parts:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - WHAT: What behavior do you want to see?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - HOW: How should the employee do it?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: What verbiage or action should they use?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - WHEN: When should the behavior happen?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - PRACTICE: How did the employee do when practicing?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The Diamond also reinforces: Document, Demonstrate, Duplicate.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should use the Management Diamond when the manager needs to teach a specific behavior, prepare for a difficult conversation, role-play a skill, or gain employee commitment.
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: 4.2 How to prepare for difficult conversations

segments.text: Before a difficult conversation, Ask Bubbles should help the manager prepare by answering:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: What is the exact behavior or result that needs to change?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Is this a skill gap, knowledge gap, confidence gap, effort gap, policy issue, or leadership issue?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: What is the correct behavior the manager wants to see?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Can the manager demonstrate the correct behavior?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: What role-play scenario will prove understanding?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Does this need coaching, EPP, DPOA, or leadership review?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A difficult conversation should not begin with frustration.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should identify root cause before recommending the next step.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Common root causes and best responses:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Signs: employee tries but sounds awkward, misses words, struggles with objections.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Response: demonstrate, role-play, observe, follow up.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Signs: employee does not know promo, product, policy, or tool.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Response: retrain, verify understanding, quiz or demonstrate, follow up.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Signs: employee avoids asking, drops offer after first hesitation, says they feel pushy.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Response: safe role-play, tougher scenarios, praise progress, observe live interaction.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Signs: employee knows what to do but does not do it, refuses tools, shows no improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Response: document, set non-negotiable expectations, consider EPP or DPOA.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Signs: manager does not coach in the moment, fails to follow up, does not use reports, allows standards to slide.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Response: Management Diamond, EPP, clear daily/shift expectations, DM follow-up.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Signs: attendance, dress code, standards of conduct, unauthorized action, refusal to follow direction, safety violation.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - Response: DPOA or leadership review depending on severity.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Respectful performance conversations are direct without being personal.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The manager should talk about behavior, expectations, and impact.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: I am going to show you how to do it, then we will practice it together, and I will follow up by [timeframe]."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Respectful does not mean soft or unclear.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should include a commitment step in every Management Diamond.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "Tell me what you will do differently on your next client interaction."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "What part do you need more practice with?"
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - "How will I know you are applying it?"
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: A better commitment is: "On my next client, I will ask one results-based question, make a relevant recommendation using the Routine Mat, and use ASTC if they hesitate."
segments.label: legacy_specific

chunks.locator: Diamond A – Spa and Routine Mat consistency

segments.text: "Recommend Spa Wellness and use the Routine Mat to educate clients on a complete routine."
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: "Start with open-ended questions about the client’s goals, skin, schedule, or results.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Use the Routine Mat to show the full routine.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: Explain what each recommended product or service is and what it does.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Tie Spa to the client’s goal, then complete the engagement or plant the seed."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Spa and Routine Mat behaviors improve client education, client results, Spa %, PPTA, OTC, and overall revenue.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: They also make recommendations feel relevant instead of random."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Every eligible client interaction, especially new clients, re-tours, current members, clients using sunless or spa, and clients who mention results or skincare needs."
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: "Role-play a client who says they only came to tan, a client who says they already have lotion, and a client who is curious but hesitant about Spa."
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: Diamond B – Club Close and BHOW

segments.text: "Present memberships top-down using BHOW and confidently handle hesitations with ASTC."
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: "Ask discovery questions, re-tour when appropriate, present the best membership option first, use BHOW to show value, explain savings and benefits, then use ASTC if the client hesitates.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: Save discounts or promotions as a closing tool rather than leading with the cheapest option."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Memberships create long-term clients, improve EFT revenue, increase future upgrade and product opportunities, and give clients the best value when presented correctly."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Every new client, non-member, expiring package, paid-in-full client, frozen/unfrozen membership opportunity, upgrade opportunity, and lower-level member who would benefit from a higher value option."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Role-play a client who says it is too expensive, a client who does not want automatic billing, a client who only wants one visit, and a current member who does not see value in upgrading."
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: Diamond C – Retention conversation for cancel/freeze/downgrade requests

segments.text: "Before processing a cancellation, downgrade, or freeze, ask discovery questions and present the most helpful option based on the client’s needs."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: How did your experience with us make you feel?
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Based on the answers, present options such as downgrade, freeze, or cancellation in a helpful order.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Explain value, future pricing, and product discount benefits where applicable."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Retention conversations protect EFT revenue, show care for the client, and prevent employees from treating account changes as a transaction instead of a service opportunity."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Anytime a client requests to cancel, freeze, downgrade, stop tanning, or says they are unsure about continuing."
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: "Role-play a client who wants to cancel because they are busy, a client who says they are not using the membership, and a client who is unhappy with results."
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: Diamond D – Manager correcting behavior in the moment

segments.text: "Correct missed behaviors during the shift instead of waiting until later or hoping the employee fixes it."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Observe the interaction, note the missed behavior, coach immediately after the client leaves when possible, demonstrate the correct verbiage, role-play once, then observe the next one or two interactions.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Document the coaching and follow-up in the shift summary or coaching planner."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Telling an employee later does not change the next client interaction.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Immediate coaching protects the client experience and teaches the behavior while it is fresh."
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "Every shift, especially when MSB, CES, ASTC, BHOW, Routine Mat, Spa, eyewear, tours, re-tours, or closing behaviors are missed."
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: "Role-play a manager coaching a TC after the TC skips eyewear, fails to recommend Spa, or drops the membership conversation after hesitation."
segments.label: methodology

chunks.locator: 5.1 When an EPP should be created

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should recommend an EPP when the issue requires a formal improvement or development plan rather than a single coaching form.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - employee is on an underperformance list or consistently missing expectations;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - employee is not showing improvement efforts;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - productivity remains low because required behaviors are not being demonstrated;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - employee is moving into a leadership role and needs a structured development plan;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - ASD, SDIT, SD, TSD, or DMIT needs documented leadership development;
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: - leadership behaviors such as delegation, accountability, global awareness, autonomy, time management, bench development, training, or follow-up are not consistent;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - a manager is not coaching, role-playing, or holding the team accountable;
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: - salon results are affected by weak execution, training, bench, or leadership routines.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: An EPP should not be used as a substitute for a DPOA when the issue is clearly a policy violation or serious misconduct.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: When the issue is both performance and policy-related, Ask Bubbles should recommend leadership review before choosing the form.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Used when a consultant is not consistently executing MSB, CES, ASTC, Routine Mat, BHOW, recommendations, closing, tours, re-tours, or productivity expectations.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Used when a Salon Director is not meeting leadership, revenue, bench, training, development, salon operations, or accountability expectations.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: Used when a training leader is expected to demonstrate higher-level leadership traits such as communication, competency, fairness, motivation, accountability, strategic thinking, and ability to develop other leaders.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Used when an employee is ready for next steps and the plan documents growth expectations, not corrective action.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Use placeholders or live employee details only when creating an actual document.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: For management, include client satisfaction, leadership, planning and execution, business requirements, sales development, team building, coaching, and operational standards.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: List real strengths so the plan is balanced and motivating.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Strengths may include reliability, positive influence, consistency, cleanliness ownership, strong client rapport, willingness to help, personal productivity, or leadership potential.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: List the top two or three biggest areas needing improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Do not create a long list that cannot be managed.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Summarize trends without dumping raw reports.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Use Daily Stats, Bonus Viewer, productivity reports, coaching history, shift observations, and salon goals to explain the pattern.
segments.label: ambiguous

segments.text: Include what the employee believes they do well and where they need improvement.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: List specific tasks, behaviors, role-plays, observations, and metrics.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: The plan must say what the employee will do and what the manager will do.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Include a re-evaluation point and interim follow-up cadence.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: State how progress will be checked and documented.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Employee and supervisor confirm the plan was discussed and the employee will participate.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Document objectives met, not met, and next action.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: EPP goals should be behavior-based and measurable.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Ask Bubbles should connect metrics to behaviors.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: "During every membership opportunity, [Employee] will present the best-fit membership top-down using BHOW, use ASTC for hesitations, and complete the engagement or plant the seed.

chunks.locator: 10.7 Final operating rule for Ask Bubbles

segments.text: When helping with performance management, Ask Bubbles should think in this order:
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Classify the issue: skill, knowledge, confidence, effort, policy, or leadership.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Choose the lowest appropriate rung on the performance management ladder.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Translate the issue into observable behavior.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Connect the behavior to client experience, productivity, revenue, team standards, or policy.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Provide the exact coaching or accountability language.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Include role-play when the issue is skill or confidence.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Escalate when the issue is repeated, policy-based, serious, or not improving.
segments.label: methodology

segments.text: Keep the tone direct, respectful, and Sun Tan City-specific.
segments.label: legacy_specific

segments.text: The purpose of this framework is to help Ask Bubbles act like a strong Sun Tan City leader: clear expectations, active coaching, real role-play, documented follow-up, fair accountability, and no emotional decisions.
